 DES MOINES, Iowa — The Iowa Insurance Division is warning Medicare beneficiaries about scams during open enrollment as people choose health insurance plans for 2027.
 “Open enrollment season for Iowans means it’s scam season for criminals,” said Attorney General Brenna Bird. “If you or someone you love is on Medicare, please be very careful of Medicare scams. If someone is calling you about Medicare, it’s almost definitely a scam because Medicare does not initiate calls to people directly. ” 
 The state's Senior Health Insurance Information Program and Senior Medicare Patrol (SHIIP-SMP) say scammers are targeting people with fraudulent insurance offers, phishing text messages and calls impersonating Medicare representatives.
 They say advances in artificial intelligence and phone number spoofing are making these types of scams even more difficult to recognize. 
 “Medicare fraud is not just a financial crime against the government – it directly harms Iowans,” said Kristin Griffith, SHIIP-SMP director. “When a scammer steals your Medicare number, they can submit fraudulent Medicare claims, leaving you unable to get legitimate care when you need it most.”
 Thousands of Iowans face Medicare plan changes
 The warning comes as more than 87,000 Iowa Medicare beneficiaries have received notices that their current Medicare Advantage, Cost or prescription drug plans are being canceled or discontinued in the coming year.
 According to the Iowa Insurance Division, the changes include the cancellation of Wellmark and Medica Medicare Advantage PPO plans that provided in-network access to the Mayo Clinic.
 Beneficiaries whose Medicare Advantage plans are canceled may qualify for special protections allowing them to purchase certain Medicare Supplement policies without medical underwriting.
 Medicare open enrollment runs through December 7. Those losing their plans have until December 31 to select replacement coverage without a gap beginning January 1. A special enrollment period extends through February 28, 2027, for affected beneficiaries.
 Officials encourage Iowans to carefully review notices from their current insurers and compare their coverage options.
 Common Medicare scams
 The Iowa Insurance Division identified several scams beneficiaries should watch for:
 New Medicare cards: Scammers claim beneficiaries must obtain new plastic or chip-enabled Medicare cards. Officials say Medicare cards do not expire and are not being replaced with those types of cards.
 Threats of canceled coverage: Callers threaten to terminate benefits unless recipients provide Medicare numbers or personal information.
 Promises of special benefits: Fraudulent advertisements offer cash cards, free medical equipment or improved coverage in exchange for Medicare information.
 Officials recommend treating Medicare numbers like credit card information and never sharing them with someone making unsolicited contact.
 Beneficiaries should avoid suspicious links in emails and text messages and verify information directly through Medicare.gov or by calling 1-800-MEDICARE (1-800-633-4227).
 Where to get help
 Iowans who suspect their Medicare information has been compromised or notice unfamiliar charges on a Medicare Summary Notice or Explanation of Benefits should report the activity.
 The Iowa Senior Medicare Patrol provides free, confidential assistance to help beneficiaries investigate suspicious claims and protect their coverage.
 Residents can call 1-800-351-4664 or report suspected fraud through the Iowa SHIIP-SMP website .
 Information about affected plans, enrollment deadlines and available counseling services is also available at shiip.iowa.gov .
